## Open

### F-227 — The flow list did not contain the execution its own call had just served

> _2026-09-21 · realm/blong-gateway · open_

`realm/blong-gateway`'s diagram spec flaked in CI and locally on `blong.flow.find`: the flow page's
table still showed "Nothing observed yet" seven seconds after the spec had served
`gateway.bundle.find` — the very execution it then looked for. Measured with a probe inside the
spec: `executionsInDom: 0`, `emptyMessages: 1`, `errorText: null`, so the read had not failed — it
was an answer that simply did not contain the row. The page reads once (`useRealmRead` re-reads only
when its parameters change) and nothing re-reads, so a second answer has to be asked for; a reload
keeps the session and the permissions (`token/restore`), which is how the spec asks for one. Two
wrong diagnoses were ruled out with the same probe: the filter is not the problem (once the answer
is in the table the kind's row appears), and the first row being another spec's execution was the
older failure (`gateway.subscription.find`), not this one.

The spec now retries producing-and-reading as a pair (`expect(...).toPass`) — five clean suite runs
where it had been two in three flaking.

Still open, and the real defect: the service's list lags the call that produced the entry, or the
read is served from a snapshot, so a caller cannot rely on "I called it, therefore it is listed".
Worth looking at when the ledger publishes and how `blong.flow.find` assembles its answer, and at
whether a page that lists executions should re-read when it is shown rather than only when it is
first opened.

### F-246 — Finding why a realm handler's progress is invisible

> _2026-09-23 · realm/blong-gateway · open_

Four turns went into answering "why is the diagram empty" for a handler that announces five
checkpoints and one decision. What unblocked it: asserting on **records**, not on `$meta`. Three
traps, each of which cost a run: - A test handler's `$meta` is **not** the object the called handler
receives (`assert` on `$meta.checkpoints` after calling through `handler()` reported `[]` while the
handler had been given its own). Assert on the handler's effect, not on the caller's object. - The
framework's retention cache is the fastest witness for "did this reach the log": a 15-line node
script over `cacheRecordIds` + `openCache` from `core/semantic-log/src/cache.ts` scanned 5056
records in a second and proved 0 carried `progress` — faster and more decisive than any browser
rerun. - The browser page's handler hook (`window.__blongHandler`) is installed when the app
_mounts_, not when the document loads, so `page.evaluate` straight after `reload()` reads
`undefined`; wait for the portal menubar first. And the hook is off unless the suite's
`index.browser.ts` sets `integration.ui.portal.portal.testHook` — the gateway suite did not.

### F-250 — A capture that pins the first execution it finds is flaky

> _2026-09-23 · realm/blong-gateway · open_

observedMergeFlow pins rows.filter({hasText: REALM_KIND}).first() after triggering a merge, but the
retry loop runs the merge repeatedly and the list may hold several executions from the same process,
so the row it reads is not necessarily the one it just made: the artifact compare then fails with a
diagram produced by another execution (or by an older shape). Pin the execution explicitly - the
highest ULID id, which is the newest - instead of taking the first row.

### F-346 — gateway.application.register mints a random secret

> _2026-10-04 · realm/blong-gateway · open_

A matrix fixture needs a secret it can write into a feature file, and the register handler generates
a random one and rotates the previous active credential, so the application matrix could not be
seeded through it. Added adapter/dbTest/gatewayApplicationMerge.ts (gateway.application.merge), a
dev-only bulk merge that takes the clientId and secret and writes the resource, the application row
and the clientSecret credential.

## Resolved

### F-454 — The rate probe window rolled under its own three calls

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-gateway · resolved_

The gateway rate probe asserts that of three metered calls the third is blocked. The counter is
keyed by the window it falls in, `Math.floor(now / rateWindowSec)`, so three calls that straddle a
boundary read a fresh counter and the third is allowed: CI failed while the same test passed
locally, and a wall-clock window is the only nondeterminism in the path. The fixture now declares
`rateWindowSec: 3600`, a window that cannot roll during a probe; the window length is not what the
test asserts.

The fixture now declares rateWindowSec 3600, so the three calls of the probe cannot straddle a
window boundary; the gateway suite passes 21/21.
